text:
Meera Patel: quick RFC follow-up — proposing a tiny "pilot-adapter" layer between the edge router and variant backends to unify pilot traffic, probes, and fast-fail behavior. TL;DR: single interface that handles routing for pilot/experiment traffic, health probes, short-circuit fallbacks, and emits rollout metadata headers. want feedback on tradeoffs and where to put state.
Sam Li: sounds useful. is this an extra hop on the critical path? latency budget concerns.
Meera Patel: yep extra hop but should be minimal — adapter runs colocated in same process space as router (option A) or as a light sidecar (option B). option A: inline calls, no extra TCP hop. option B: isolation and easier rollout. tradeoff: fault domain vs latency.
Nguyen Tran: agree latency matters. can the adapter be a decision cache + policy engine and then write a small routing token so router still forwards directly? that would keep fast path but still centralize policy.
Meera Patel: good point. design sketch: adapter exports a tiny API: -> decide(request_meta) returns {variant, route_meta, fallback_policy_id}. router can call decide with sampling key. we can cache decisions for N ms keyed by session/prefix to avoid repeated compute.
Carla Gomez: how do we handle stateful sessions and KV cache affinity? if pilot traffic lands on different variant we could lose KV cache hits and increase latency.
Meera Patel: plan is to prefer session affinity when present. adapter returns affinity hints. also we can add a soft-warmup: before switching a user, send a probe request to new variant to prefill KV cache (optional).
Ravi Singh: analytics question — we need to preserve experiment attribution when we fall back automatically. if someone is in A but we fail them to B for safety, analytics should note cause = failover, not original assignment.
Meera Patel: yes — the adapter must annotate responses with rollout-trace headers and a small event to the rollout telemetry stream: {assignment, final_variant, reason}. gives us signal to separate assignment vs fallback.
Sam Li: config idea:
```
pilot_adapter:
  policies:
    - id: fast-fail-quick
      max_error_rate: 0.05
      fallback: reduce_traffic
      probe: {type: health_check, path: /probe, timeout_ms: 200}
    - id: gradual-warmup
      ramp_seconds: 3600
      fallback: redirect_to_stable
```
Meera Patel: exactly. open Q: where to evaluate error_rate? within adapter (local window) or centrally by telemetry service? local window faster but can be noisy.
Nguyen Tran: local window + global rollup. adapter emits per-policy metrics so central system can override and push forced-fallback via control-plane flag.
Carla Gomez: how do we ensure failures in adapter don't take down router? must be sandboxed and have a very strict CPU/memory cap and fallback to passthrough default.
Meera Patel: yes default behavior is passthrough: if adapter fails (panic/timeouts) router should route using last-known policy or default stable variant. fail-open vs fail-closed needs policy-level setting.
ops-bot: deploy note — feature-flag gate exists: rollout.pilot_adapter.enabled = false by default. toggle path: /flags/rollout/pilot_adapter
Ravi Singh: testing plan: 1) local benchtop perf with synthetic traffic, 2) e2e with a single region pilot, 3) small % global experiment. need chaos tests where adapter crashes and where probe services return malformed responses.
Sam Li: also need a migration path from current fallback-router. maybe compatibility shim so existing rules import into pilot_adapter policy format.
Meera Patel: good call. i'll draft a short RFC doc with interface proto, config schema, and rollout checklist. questions to settle:
- inline vs sidecar default? (latency vs isolation)
- local vs central error windows
- attribution event schema
- warmup probe semantics
Please ping if you want to co-author. @Sam Li @Nguyen Tran @Carla Gomez :thumbsup:
Sam Li: +1, will add perf numbers.
Nguyen Tran: +1, i can model telemetry thresholds.
Carla Gomez: +1, will write affinity/kv notes.
Ravi Singh: assigning followups: i'll own telemetry event spec. ops-bot: create a ticket? :slightly_smiling_face:
ops-bot: ticket created: INFRA-1427 — pilot adapter RFC + rollout checklist (link: https://tickets.internal/INFRA-1427)
